x: Bill Lucas came next and he was followed by Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker, who came in together, with Bob Taylor and Ted Stimpson close behind, and this laid the foundation of our win in the team race over our old and friendly rivals. P.

John Bromley, who is now qualified to represent us, having resigned from his Northern club, Winton Harriers, was another to run well, and here again we have a most useful recruit to our ranks. We were pleased to see Eddie Short, who is now an officer in the R.A.F. and stationed at Halton Camp, turni…
Abbott, who does most of his running for London University, finished a good second, with our new member, P.

The Middlesex race was held at Trent Park, Cockfosters, and here again our lads did quite well running for their second-claim club, Cadogan A.C. Bob Taylor did not run up to expectations in finishing 21st, but P.
Team Result.—1, Southgate H and Royal Grammar School (High Wycombe), 108; 3, Thames Valley H., 109; Belgrave H., 152. Junior (5 miles).—10, P.
This was held at Maidenhead on November 8th and as in 1949 at the same venue, we had the second man home in the individual race. P.

Notable absentees included previous winners in Vern Blowfield and Len Herbert, and we had Eric Herbert running in the Civil Service race on the same day. Len Adams, who has recently married, and Archie Bedford, also P.

As the winning team is barred from competing again, it will be seen that fresh men have constantly to be found and we think our post-war record speaks for itself. We thought we should improve on last year's 7th position, but as we were without P.
